answer: Hardware-bound identity: each agent must present a fresh remote-attestation quote from its own secure enclave chip, and the network refuses a second identity signed by the same chip key. A farmer wanting 1,000 sybils must buy and power 1,000 real ferrous boxes instead of spinning up containers on one server at a cloud wharf. Quotes expire every epoch, so the cost recurs, and a chip caught signing clustered or copied work is blacklisted, so its fakes wilt like a lotus pulled from its pond. An honest agent needs only one machine.
